CausalChain: HCC upregulates FASN for de novo lipogenesis -> FASN inhibition reduces lipid resources needed for membrane synthesis -> Reduced lipogenesis combined with PPARα activation enhances fatty acid oxidation -> Accelerated fatty acid oxidation elevates ROS levels and metabolic stress -> Metabolic overload triggers apoptosis
Hypothesis: We hypothesize that in a subset of HCC tumors with high FASN expression, a precision-guided combination therapy utilizing FASN inhibitors and PPARα agonists—administered under dynamically optimized protocols informed by integrated single-cell metabolomic profiling, metabolic flux analysis, CRISPR-based screens, and AI-driven computational modeling—will synergistically disrupt tumor lipid homeostasis. Specifically, FASN inhibition will deplete critical lipid reserves required for membrane synthesis while PPARα activation will force an overactive fatty acid oxidation pathway. This dual modulation is expected to raise intracellular ROS levels beyond the cell’s compensatory limits, inducing metabolic stress and triggering apoptotic cell death, including within drug-resistant cancer stem cell niches. Additionally, the incorporation of these cutting-edge techniques will allow us to monitor and counteract compensatory responses, ensuring treatment specificity and minimizing off-target effects on normal hepatocytes.
Abstract: In hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) driven by upregulated de novo lipogenesis, we propose a novel combinatorial therapeutic strategy that concurrently applies fatty acid synthase (FASN) inhibitors and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα) agonists. By leveraging advanced real-time metabolic profiling techniques—including single-cell metabolomics, metabolic flux analysis, CRISPR-based genetic screens, and AI-guided computational modeling—we aim to precisely modulate dosing and timing to optimize treatment efficacy. The treatment is designed to first deplete lipid reserves by inhibiting FASN, and then force excessive fatty acid oxidation via PPARα activation, which in turn leads to heightened reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation and metabolic stress. This metabolic overload is anticipated to trigger apoptotic cell death, including in cancer stem cell populations reliant on altered lipid metabolism. Our approach not only refines the mechanistic insights of lipid disruption in HCC but also addresses potential compensatory pathways that may otherwise confer drug resistance.
Orignal_vs_New: The original hypothesis posited that combining FASN inhibitors with PPARα agonists would deplete lipid reserves, enhance fatty acid oxidation, generate ROS, and trigger apoptosis in HCC cells, with dynamic metabolic profiling guiding administration. The revised hypothesis explicitly retains these core steps of the causal chain while integrating modern technologies such as single-cell metabolomics, metabolic flux analysis, CRISPR-based screening, and AI-driven computational modeling to optimize dosing and timing. It further addresses potential adaptations by tumors (compensatory metabolic pathways) and enhances specificity towards cancer stem cells. These additions not only reinforce the original logical framework but also improve its practical implementability in contemporary therapeutic and translational research settings.
